chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It was said to him, 'Do you see the one who performs Hajj on behalf of his father, or his mother, or his brother, or others, should he say something?' He said, 'Yes. He should say when he enters the state of Ihram: O Allah, whatever hardship, or untidiness, or difficulty befalls me, reward so-and-so for it, and reward me for my performance on his behalf.'

key_terms.فُلَاناً: so-and-so (the person on whose behalf the Hajj is performed)

ai.seo_question: What should one say when performing Hajj on behalf of someone else?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific supplication recited during the Ihram state when performing Hajj on behalf of another, highlighting the Shia scholarly understanding of substituting worship (Hajj al-Tamattu' or Hajj al-Ifrad for others). The supplication requests that Allah transfer the physical hardships (nasab) and difficulties endured by the performer to the deceased or absent person, while ensuring the performer receives the reward for their effort. This reflects the principle of vicarious worship, where the spiritual merit is transferred to the intended beneficiary while the physical burden is borne by the agent.
